lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How many everyday business tasks are really just a person moving information from one screen to another? That's the kind of work Antoine now does as an intern at La Caisse.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So he's automating the boring parts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pretty much. He joined as a Software Developer Intern in the Digital and Analytics Solutions group, and his role starts from August 2026. The work centers on business-process automation using SharePoint, TypeScript, C sharp and dot NET.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is it all about building new things?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's an integration side too. He contributes to API integrations and to the migration work away from SnapLogic, which is a tool that connects different systems. Think of it as rewiring the plumbing between applications.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And who tells him what to build?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A cross-functional team. Together they turn business needs into clear application and integration requirements, so what gets built matches what people actually do all day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds like a nice mix of coding and talking to people.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's the mix Antoine was looking for: software, system integration and requirements work, in the same shape as his earlier platform and backend roles, now in an institutional setting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Does he bring anything with him from those earlier roles?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. CI/CD and platform habits from his secure cloud work, with GitLab pipelines, Kubernetes on GKE and Terraform. Reproducible setups and clear hand-offs from teaching at Polytechnique and ETS. And structured error handling in dot NET from his time at IONODES, where Serilog and Sentry fed production diagnostics.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The offices carry a lot of Quebec art, which gives the place its own character. The full post has the finance-month flyer and links to those earlier stories.
